2001 05 09 #2001 |checkboxAutoTeams=Yes |checkbox2=No |role=Mid |issub1=No |istrainee1=No |issub2=No |istrainee2=No |issub3=No |istrainee3=No |issub4=No |istrainee4=No |issub5=No |istrainee5=No |checkbox3=No |stream=https://www.twitch.tv/jojopyun |twitter=jojopyunlol |instagram=jojopyun |lolpros=https://lolpros.gg/player/jojopyun |deeplol=https://www.deeplol.gg/pro/Jojopyun |dpmlol=https://dpm.lol/pro/Jojopyun |checkboxSuppressOrgNavbox=No |otherwikis=Fortnite |checkboxSBS=Yes |checkboxTOCR=No |checkboxIsSub=No |checkbox-res=No |checkboxPrev=No }} == Biography == Jojopyun was born in Toronto, Ontario. === 2020 Season === Jojopyun began playing ''League of Legends'' seriously in 2020 and quickly became a highly-touted solo queue prodigy who briefly played in the North American amateur scene for the short-lived [[Noble Esports]]. He was then picked up as a substitute for [[Zenith Esports]], although he did not play for the team. At the end of the season, the roster of Zenith Esports was acquired by [[Evil Geniuses]] to form [[Evil Geniuses Prodigies]]. Jojopyun's solo queue ranking qualified him for [[NASG 2020]], but he was too young to attend the event. Nonetheless, he attracted the attention of Evil Geniuses' new coach [[Peter Dun]], who believed Jojopyun was a "real person to look out for" and that he "[could] be insane long term."[https://twitter.com/IWDominate/status/1518292584304717826 IWDominate's Tweet] ''twitter.com'' === 2021 Season === Due to Peter Dun's scouting, Jojopyun was signed as the [[Evil Geniuses Academy]] mid laner for the 2021 season, being too young to play in the LCS. Despite high expectations, the team performed poorly during the [[NA Academy League/2021 Season/Spring Season|Spring split]], finishing 10th place with a 2-7 record. However, the team improved rapidly and finished 4th in [[LCS Proving Grounds/2021 Season/Spring|Proving Grounds]]. Jojopyun gained a reputation as an aggressive player who would play a feast or famine style, leading some commentators to describe him as a "coin flip" player, similar to the Evil Geniuses LCS mid laner [[Jiizuke]]. Despite inconsistencies, Tim Sevenhuysen ranked Jojopyun as the second most promising upcoming talent, behind only [[Kenvi]].[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lF7FOvGUJFI NA's Top 10 Prospects - The best upcoming League of Legends rookies in North America] ''youtube.com'' === 2022 Season === Jojopyun was promoted to the Evil Geniuses LCS team in a move that was controversial because the previous mid laner, Jiizuke, was coming off of a career best split in which he won 1st All Pro Team. [[Doublelift]] suggested that LCS teams were more concerned with "developing talent" than winning, a comment that seemed to be aimed at Evil Geniuses, which was also fielding a young bot laner in [[Danny (Kyle Sakamaki)|Danny]]. With the team rounded out by veteran talents [[Impact]], [[Inspired]], and [[Vulcan (Philippe Laflamme)|Vulcan]], Evil Geniuses was expected to perform well, but was not considered a favorite for the LCS title over reigning champion [[100 Thieves]] or star-studded [[Team Liquid]]. The team took off to a hot start during [[LCS 2022 Lock In]], going undefeated in group stages and the first two rounds of the knockout stage. However, Evil Geniuses lost to Team Liquid 0-3 in the finals, with Jojopyun in particular being criticized for his performance against [[Bjergsen]]. During the [[LCS 2022 Spring]] regular season, Evil Geniuses continued to struggle against top teams, losing every game against Team Liquid, 100 Thieves, and [[Cloud9]]. Jojopyun became known as a lane dominant player, leading the league's mid laners in gold and creep score at 10 minutes. However, he often struggled to translate lane leads to later success, winding up with low kill participation and a high deaths in side lanes. Some fans called for him to be replaced by veteran free agents such as [[Jensen]] or [[Nisqy]], while others believed he showed promise as a rookie. The team finished with a 9-9 regular season record, only one win above being eliminated from playoffs. In playoffs, few predicted the team to do well, with most attention on Team Liquid, 100 Thieves, and Cloud9. However, Evil Geniuses surprised many when they took Team Liquid to five games in the first upper bracket series. Evil Geniuses ultimately lost the series and went to the loser's bracket, where the team continued to improve. After defeating [[FlyQuest]] 3-1, they swept Cloud9, Team Liquid, and 100 Thieves one after another to win the split. Jojopyun became the youngest player to win the LCS. EG represented North America at [[MSI 2022]]. The team reached the semifinals before being eliminated by [[Royal Never Give Up]]. During the [[LCS 2022 Summer|Summer Split]], EG secured a 1st-place finish in the regular season, with Jojopyun earning 1st All-Pro honors. Despite their regular season dominance, the team eventually finished 3rd in the playoffs, which nonetheless earned them a spot in the [[Worlds 2022 Play-In]]. EG successfully navigated the Play-In stage, notably sweeping the LEC representatives [[MAD Lions]] 3-0 in the qualifying round. However, during the [[2022 Season World Championship/Main Event|Main Event]], the team was eliminated with a 1-5 record in a group featuring [[JD Gaming]], [[G2 Esports]], and [[DWG KIA]]. === 2023 Season === For the [[LCS 2023 Spring|2023 Spring Split]], Jojopyun remained with Evil Geniuses. After a lackluster regular season and an early knockout in the [[LCS 2023 Spring Playoffs|Spring Playoffs]], the team underwent a massive overhaul. Heading into the summer, Evil Geniuses completely revamped their roster, retaining only Jojopyun as the starting mid laner while surrounding him with a new supporting cast. Under this new leadership role, Jojopyun reached a career peak during the [[LCS 2023 Summer|2023 Summer Split]]. He delivered a dominant individual performance that earned him both his second 1st All-Pro Team honor and the LCS Most Valuable Player award. Despite his MVP-caliber play, the team was unable to secure an international spot, finishing 5th-6th in the [[LCS 2023 Championship]] after a loss to Team Liquid. === 2024 Season === Jojopyun joined the [[Cloud9]] roster for the [[LCS/2024 Season|2024 season]], forming what many fans and analysts considered a "superteam" alongside [[Fudge]], [[Blaber]], [[Berserker (Kim Min-cheol)|Berserker]], and his former teammate [[Vulcan (Philippe Laflamme)|Vulcan]]. Despite being rated as the heavy favorites to dominate the league, the team struggled with consistency and failed to meet the high expectations placed upon them. During the [[LCS 2024 Spring|Spring Split]], Cloud9 finished 3rd in the playoffs after a loss to [[Team Liquid]], narrowly missing out on qualification for [[MSI 2024]]. The team's struggles continued into the [[LCS 2024 Summer|Summer Split]], where they were eventually eliminated in the lower bracket and failed to qualify for [[Worlds 2024]]. Shortly after the season concluded, Cloud9 made the shocking decision to terminate Jojopyun's contract, with subsequent reports citing internal issues regarding repeated tardiness and professional conduct. === 2025 Season === In a landmark move for North American talent, Jojopyun moved to the EMEA region to join [[Movistar KOI]] for the [[LEC/2025 Season|2025 season]]. He became the first NA-resident player to compete in the LEC. His transition was remarkably successful; after adjusting to the European meta, he led Movistar KOI to a domestic title in [[LEC/2025 Season/Spring Season|Spring 2025]], defeating G2 Esports in the grand finals. == Trivia == * His older sister, Allison, came up with his ign “jojopyun” (it’s also derived from his real name). * He is Korean-Canadian, but he doesn’t speak much Korean. Calls himself “fake Korean.” His Korean name appears to be just “Joon” which his past coach Rigby has called him. * Gained fame stream-sniping famous ''Fortnite'' streamers including Turner "Tfue" Tenny, then beating him in 1v1s, before switching to ''League of Legends''. * Attended online high school while playing professionally in LCS Academy; didn’t end up completing it. * Fourth native North American mid laner, and first Canadian mid laner, to win the LCS. ** The previous native North American LCS champions were [[Reginald]], [[Hai]], and [[Pobelter]]. * The second Canadian mid laner to attend Worlds and the first since [[bigfatlp]] in 2012. * Youngest player to win the LCS (winning at 17 years, 6 months). ** The previous record holder was [[Santorin]], who won [[NA LCS 2015 Spring Playoffs|2015 Spring]] at 17 years, 11 months. * Known for his trash talk, famously saying [https://twitter.com/jojopyunlol/status/1482511213325996033 "This is your goat??"] after defeating [[Bjergsen]] during the [[LCS 2022 Lock In]]. * Part of a select group of players called "Royal Roaders", earned after winning their rookie split in a major region (LCS Spring 2022) * Had the opportunity to join [[Liiv SANDBOX]] for the 2024 season but chose [[Cloud9]]. * Is the first and only player from North America to ever play in the LEC, as he joined [[Movistar KOI]] in [[LEC/2025_Season/Winter_Season|Winter 2025]]. * He is the first player from North America to win an LEC title, doing so in [[LEC/2025_Season/Spring_Season|Spring 2025]] as Movistar KOI took down [[G2 Esports|G2]] 3-1 in the final. === Individual Awards === * LCS Most Valuable Player (2023 Summer) * 2x LCS 1st All-Pro Team (2022 Summer, 2023 Summer) * 2x LCS 2nd All-Pro Team (2024 Spring, 2024 Summer) * LCS Rookie of the Year (2022) * LEC 1st All-Pro Team (2026 Spring) * LEC 2nd All-Pro Team (2025 Spring) {{PlayerStatsTrivia}} == Tournament Results == {{PlayerResults|show=overviewpage}} {{PlayerShowmatchResults|show=overviewpage}} {{PlayerResults1v1|show=overviewpage}} == Media == {{PlayerMedia}} === Images === {{PlayerProfileGallery}} {{PlayerPageEnd}}
